draft.title: Why businesses matter
card: Businesses add to a nation's economic and social wellbeing. Wellbeing here means how well people in the nation are able to live.
Jobs
businesses employ people. Wages let workers pay for housing, food and other needs, and work can give people a sense of purpose.
Goods and services
businesses make and sell what people need and want, such as food, clothing and transport.
Tax and new ideas
businesses and their workers pay tax, which governments can use to fund schools, hospitals and roads. Businesses also try new products and ways of working, which can improve daily life.
draft.remember: Businesses can add to wellbeing through jobs, goods and services, tax revenue and new ideas.

a.q: Mia opens a bakery in Ballarat and hires three local people. Which benefit to the nation does hiring them show?
opts: It provides jobs that give people an income
It provides tax revenue that funds new roads
It provides new ideas that start other businesses
It provides goods that people want to buy
a.why: Hiring local people creates jobs, and wages give them an income. Selling bread does provide goods, but the question asks about what hiring the three people shows.
a.clue: Look at what happens to the three local people.

b.q: A Geelong company makes a new type of recyclable packaging. It sells the packaging to food makers and pays company tax. Which pair of benefits does this show?
opts: New ideas and tax revenue
Jobs and new ideas
Goods and services and jobs
Tax revenue and jobs
b.why: A new type of packaging is a new idea, and paying company tax gives governments tax revenue. The story says nothing about hiring workers, so jobs are not shown, even though a real company would probably employ some.
b.clue: Find what the story says about something new and about paying money to government.

a.best: It provides jobs that give people an income

problems.detail: The clue ('something new and ... paying money to government') names both parts of the right pair, so a student can pick 'New ideas and tax revenue' without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate. The only problem is that question b's clue points straight to new ideas and tax revenue, giving the answer away.
